docs.title: MTHDS JSON Schema
docs.text: The MTHDS standard includes a machine-readable JSON Schema that describes the structure of .mthds files. Tools and editors can use this schema for validation, autocompletion, and documentation.

docs.title: What It Covers
docs.text:
The schema defines the complete structure of an .mthds bundle:

  • Header fields: domain, description, system_prompt, main_pipe.
  • Concept definitions: both simple (string) and structured forms, including structure fields, refines, and all field types (text, integer, number, boolean, date, datetime, time, list, dict, concept) and the choices enum mechanism.
  • Pipe definitions: all concrete pipe types with their specific fields — PipeLLM, PipeStructure, PipeFunc, PipeImgGen, PipeExtract, PipeSearch, PipeJudge, PipeDocGen, PipeCompose, PipeSequence, PipeParallel, PipeCondition, PipeBatch — plus contract-only PipeSignature sections where type is omitted. Every inputs table accepts only plain input names, matching [a-z][a-z0-9_]*.
  • Sub-pipe blueprints: the steps, branches, outcomes, and construct structures used by controllers and PipeCompose. A sequence step is either a pipe step or a binding step (from and result), while a parallel branch is always a pipe step whose batch_over is a plain name.
  • Inline model settings: the LLMSetting, ImgGenSetting, ExtractSetting, SearchSetting, JudgmentSetting, and DocGenSetting objects that can be used in place of string model references.

docs.title: Schema Version
docs.text: The schema is generated from the bundle data model of the reference implementation, and its $comment field names the implementation version it was generated from. The hosted schema is refreshed from a release of the reference implementation, and a release of the standard that changes the language usually comes before the implementation release that carries the change. Until that implementation release is published and the refreshed schema reaches this site, the hosted schema still describes the previous standard and may reject what the new one allows. The changelog entry of such a release says which of its changes the hosted schema does not describe yet, and a later release of this site publishes the schema that does.

docs.title: Where to Find It
docs.text:
The schema is distributed with the tools that use it:

  • VS Code extension — the Pipelex extension bundles the schema and uses it for autocompletion and inline validation.
  • plxt CLI — the plxt binary includes the schema for local validation.
  • pipelex-tools PyPI package — the schema is included in the Python distribution.

The schema is also hosted at a stable URL for direct use by editors and other tooling:

Hosted URL: https://mthds.ai/mthds_schema.json

docs.title: With the VS Code Extension
docs.text: The Pipelex VS Code extension includes the schema and uses it automatically for autocompletion and inline validation of .mthds files. No configuration is required.

docs.title: With Other Editors
docs.text: Any editor that supports JSON Schema for TOML can use the MTHDS schema. Configure your editor's TOML language server to associate .mthds files with the schema URL https://mthds.ai/mthds_schema.json.

docs.title: For Tooling
docs.text:
The schema can be used programmatically for:

  • Building custom validators for .mthds files.
  • Generating documentation from the schema structure.
  • Implementing autocompletion in non-VS Code editors.

For detailed guidance on building editor support, see For Implementers: Building Editor Support.

Copy Markdown

docs.title: What is MTHDS?
docs.text:
MTHDS (pronounced "methods") is an open standard for AI methods. It defines a typed language for describing what an AI should do — the data it works with, the transformations it performs, and how those transformations compose together — in plain text files that humans and machines can read.

An AI method in MTHDS is not code in the traditional sense. It is a declaration: "given this kind of input, produce that kind of output, using this approach." An agent or runner decides how to execute it. The method author decides what it means.

docs.title: Why a New Standard?
docs.text:
Current approaches to AI workflows each solve part of the problem but leave significant gaps:

Code (Python, frameworks) provides full control, typed outputs, and testability. But the business logic that matters — the actual extraction, analysis, or reasoning steps — is buried in infrastructure code. Domain experts cannot read or iterate on it.

Natural-language instructions (prompts, skills) are the opposite: easy to write and human-readable. But they carry no typed outputs, no validation, and no guaranteed output structure. The agent reinterprets them at every invocation.

Automation platforms (Zapier, Make, n8n) connect APIs through visual, GUI-based editors designed for deterministic workflows — not for AI. AI capabilities were bolted on after the fact. Their interfaces are built for human point-and-click editing, not for agents to read or compose programmatically. And when workflows require multi-step cognitive work — extraction, analysis, synthesis — these platforms lack the conceptual typing system to validate what flows between steps.

MTHDS provides the missing combination: a declarative language that is typed enough to validate, structured enough to compose, and readable enough for domain experts to understand. The method separates what a workflow does from how it is executed, analogous to how SQL separates data queries from storage engines.

docs.title: Agents as First-Class Participants
docs.text:
MTHDS gives agents the ability to discover, compose, and execute structured AI methods. But agents are not limited to execution. Because .mthds files are plain text with typed structure, agents can also build new methods, modify existing ones, and extend the ecosystem. An agent can search the Know-How Graph for methods by typed signature ("I have a Document, I need a NonCompeteClause"), compose them into multi-step workflows, create new methods that fill gaps in the graph, and execute them with validated data flow. Methods are artifacts agents can create, not just consume.

The language reads close to natural language and is designed to transcribe business logic. Concepts like ContractClause, CandidateProfile, or Joke carry business meaning directly — they are not programming abstractions but representations of real domain knowledge. A Pipe that declares inputs = { doc = "ContractClause" } and output = "NonCompeteClause" reads as a business statement, not as code. Domain experts can read and understand .mthds files without programming skills, making methods a shared artifact between technical and non-technical teams.

docs.title: The Two Pillars
docs.text: MTHDS has two complementary halves, designed so you can start with one and add the other when you need it.

docs.title: Pillar 1 — The Language
docs.text:
The .mthds file format. Everything you need to define typed data and AI transformations in a single file.

A .mthds file is a valid TOML document with structure and meaning layered on top. If you know TOML, you already know the syntax. Inside a file, you define:

  • Concepts — typed data declarations. A concept is a named type that describes a kind of data: a ContractClause, a CandidateProfile, a Joke. Concepts can have internal structure (fields with types like text, integer, boolean, list, number, date, datetime, time, dict, and concept) or they can be simple semantic labels. Concepts can refine other concepts — NonCompeteClause refines ContractClause, meaning it can be used anywhere a ContractClause is expected.

  • Pipes — typed transformations. A concrete pipe declares its inputs (concepts), its output (a concept), and its type — what kind of work it does. A contract-only signature omits type until it is implemented. MTHDS defines operators (PipeLLM for language model generation, PipeStructure for turning text into a structured concept, PipeFunc for Python functions, PipeImgGen for image generation, PipeExtract for document extraction, PipeSearch for web search, PipeJudge for verdicts on closed questions, PipeCompose for templating and assembly) and controllers (PipeSequence for sequential steps, PipeParallel for concurrent branches, PipeCondition for conditional routing, PipeBatch for mapping over lists).

  • Domains — namespaces that organize concepts and pipes. A domain like legal.contracts tells you what a bundle is about and prevents naming collisions between unrelated definitions.

A single .mthds file — called a bundle — works on its own. No manifest, no package, no configuration. This is the starting point for learning and prototyping.

Learn the Language

docs.title: Pillar 2 — The Package System
docs.text:
The infrastructure for distributing and composing methods at scale.

When a standalone bundle is not enough — when you want to share methods, depend on other people's work, or control which methods are public — you add a METHODS.toml manifest. This turns a directory of bundles into a package: a distributable unit with a globally unique address, semantic versioning, declared dependencies, and explicit exports.

Packages are stored in Git repositories. The package address (e.g., github.com/acme/legal-tools) doubles as the fetch location — no upload step, no proprietary hosting. A lock file (methods.lock) pins exact versions with tree digests and semantic fingerprints for verifiable installs.

Cross-package references use the -> syntax: scoring_lib->scoring.compute_weighted_score reads as "from the scoring_lib dependency, get compute_weighted_score in the scoring domain." The separator was chosen for readability by non-technical audiences — arrows are intuitive, visually distinct from dots, and universally understood.

The Package System

docs.title: Core Concepts at a Glance
docs.text: Term What it is Analogy Concept A typed data declaration — the kinds of data that flow through pipes. A form with typed fields. Pipe A typed transformation — declares inputs, output, and what kind of work it does. A processing step in a workflow. Domain A namespace that groups related concepts and pipes. A folder that organizes related definitions. Bundle A single .mthds file. The authoring unit. A source file. Package A directory with a METHODS.toml manifest and one or more bundles. The distribution unit. A versioned library.

docs.title: A Concrete Example
docs.text:
Here is a complete, working .mthds file:

domain      = "joke_generation"
description = "Generating one-liner jokes from topics"
main_pipe   = "generate_jokes_from_topics"

[concept.Topic]
description = "A subject or theme that can be used as the basis for a joke."
refines     = "Text"

[concept.Joke]
description = "A humorous one-liner intended to make people laugh."
refines     = "Text"

[pipe.generate_jokes_from_topics]
type        = "PipeSequence"
description = "Generate 3 joke topics and create a joke for each"
output      = "Joke[]"
steps = [
    { pipe = "generate_topics", result = "topics" },
    { pipe = "batch_generate_jokes", result = "jokes" },
]

[pipe.generate_topics]
type        = "PipeLLM"
description = "Generate 3 distinct topics suitable for jokes"
output      = "Topic[3]"
prompt      = "Generate 3 distinct and varied topics for crafting one-liner jokes."

[pipe.batch_generate_jokes]
type             = "PipeBatch"
description      = "Generate a joke for each topic"
inputs           = { topics = "Topic[]" }
output           = "Joke[]"
branch_pipe_code = "generate_joke"
input_list_name  = "topics"
input_item_name  = "topic"

[pipe.generate_joke]
type        = "PipeLLM"
description = "Write a clever one-liner joke about the given topic"
inputs      = { topic = "Topic" }
output      = "Joke"
prompt      = "Write a clever one-liner joke about $topic. Be concise and witty."

This file defines concepts (Topic and Joke, both refining the built-in Text type) and pipes: a sequence that generates topics and then batch-processes them into jokes. It works as a standalone file — save it, point a runner at it, and it runs. (A runner is any server implementing the MTHDS HTTP Runner Protocol — five routes; anyone can build one.)

docs.title: Progressive Enhancement
docs.text:
MTHDS is designed so you can start simple and add complexity only when you need it:

  1. Single file — a .mthds bundle works on its own. No configuration, no manifest, no dependencies. Define concepts and pipes, and run them.

  2. Package — add a METHODS.toml manifest to get a globally unique identity, version number, and visibility controls. Pipes become private by default; you choose what to export.

  3. Dependencies — add a [dependencies] section to compose with other packages. Reference their concepts and pipes using the -> syntax.

  4. Ecosystem — publish packages to Git repositories by pushing a tag. Registry indexes crawl and index them, enabling search and package pages with validation badges and freshness signals. At the horizon, the Know-How Graph — a typed network of AI methods, specified as a future direction — lets you ask "I have a Document, I need a NonCompeteClause" and find the pipes (or chains of pipes) that get you there.

Each layer builds on the previous one without breaking it. A standalone bundle that works today continues to work unchanged inside a package.

docs.title: What Makes MTHDS Different
docs.text:
MTHDS differs from other approaches to describing AI capabilities in three ways:

  • Typed signatures. Every pipe declares the concepts it accepts and produces. This enables semantic discovery ("I have X, I need Y") and compile-time validation of data flow — something text-based descriptions cannot provide.

  • Composition built in. Controllers (sequence, parallel, condition, batch) are part of the language, not an external orchestration layer. Multi-step methods are defined in the same file as the individual steps.

  • A real package system. Visibility controls and cross-package references are live today; versioned dependencies and lock files are fully specified and being implemented — the same infrastructure that makes code ecosystems work, applied to AI methods.

docs.title: Where to Go Next
docs.text:
• Method authors: Start with The Language to learn bundles, concepts, pipes, and domains. Then move to The Package System when you are ready to distribute.

  • Runner implementers: Start with the Specification for the normative reference on file formats, validation rules, and resolution algorithms.

  • Everyone: Write Your First Method walks you through creating a working .mthds file step by step.

Copy Markdown

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text:
Every code of the MTHDS core error registry has a page here, at the URL a problem's type names: https://mthds.ai/errors/<code>. Each page says what its code means, who must act and what to do, and gives the code's steps, parameters and templates. The Error Registry page describes the registry itself, and the HTTP Runner Protocol how a problem document carries a code.

These pages are generated from the registry's data, which is published with every release of the standard as mthds-error-registry.json. This is version 8.0.0 of the registry.

docs.title: Extension prefixes
docs.text:
A code that is not a core code starts with a registered prefix, and its page is published by the prefix's owner, under the base URL the prefix is registered with.

Prefix Owner Base URL pipelex. Pipelex https://docs.pipelex.com/errors

docs.title: request
docs.text:
The HTTP request itself, before any run.

Code Title Domain Retry Status request.malformed The request body cannot be parsed input no 422 request.invalid The request does not match the route's schema input no 422 request.too_large The request exceeds a size limit input no 413 request.not_found No such route input no 404 request.method_not_allowed The route does not accept this HTTP method input no 405 request.unsupported The request uses a form this runtime does not accept input no 422 request.idempotency_conflict The idempotency key was used for a different request input no 409 request.idempotency_key_in_use A request under this idempotency key is still running runtime yes 409 request.already_executed The request already ran and its answer is not kept input no 409 request.pipe_not_found The selected pipe is not in the method input no 422 request.pipe_ambiguous The pipe selection matches several pipes input no 422 request.pipe_unspecified No pipe is selected input no 422 request.blobs_missing The runner does not hold some files sent by hash input no 422

Credentials and permissions.

Code Title Domain Retry Status auth.missing_credential No credential was sent account no 401 auth.invalid_credential The credential was refused account no 401 auth.credential_expired The credential has expired account no 401 auth.forbidden The credential does not permit this account no 403

The account's limits.

A run's inputs.

Code Title Domain Retry Status input.missing A required input is missing input no 422 input.unexpected An input the method does not declare input no 422 input.wrong_concept An input is not the declared concept input no 422 input.wrong_multiplicity An input has the wrong number of items input no 422 input.invalid An input does not fit its concept's structure input no 422 input.file_unreadable An input file cannot be read input no 422 input.file_type_unsupported An input file's type is not supported here input no 422 input.too_large An input exceeds a size limit input no 422 input.reference_not_found An input refers to something that does not exist input no 422 input.url_unreachable An input's URL could not be fetched input yes 422

docs.title: method

docs.title: request.malformed
docs.text:
The request body cannot be parsed

Type https://mthds.ai/errors/request.malformed Family request: The HTTP request itself, before any run. Domain input: the caller acts, by changing the request or its inputs Retry no: repeating the operation fails the same way HTTP status 422 Raised as a problem document, sent as the body of an HTTP response or kept in a run's record

docs.title: What it means
docs.text: The body is not parseable JSON, a Base64 or zip payload it carries is corrupt, or a text entry holds a code point UTF-8 cannot encode. The protocol answers a malformed body with a 422.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text: Check how the client builds the body: that it serializes valid JSON, writes text in UTF-8, and encodes every Base64 entry in standard padded Base64 with its pad bits zero. Then send the request again.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
A problem carries the step aimed at whoever reads it: the first when its reader is the domain's actor, the caller, and the second for any other reader.

Reader Kind Detail The domain's actor change_input Fix the body so that it parses, then send the request again. Any other reader change_input Pass this to the caller, who must send a request body that parses.

docs.title: Detail
docs.text:
The problem's detail is written from this template, filled with the occurrence's parameters:

The runner cannot parse the request body (reason: {reason}).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Every parameter is present on every occurrence of the code.

Name Type Description reason one of not_json, not_utf8, bad_base64, bad_zip What could not be parsed: the body as JSON, a text entry as UTF-8, a Base64 entry, or a zip archive the request carries.

docs.title: request.invalid
docs.text:
The request does not match the route's schema

Type https://mthds.ai/errors/request.invalid Family request: The HTTP request itself, before any run. Domain input: the caller acts, by changing the request or its inputs Retry no: repeating the operation fails the same way HTTP status 422 Raised as a problem document, sent as the body of an HTTP response or kept in a run's record

docs.title: What it means
docs.text: The body parses, but a field fails the route's schema. A problem with several such faults carries one item per fault in errors, each naming its field in location.field. The protocol's refusals of one hash given twice with different sizes, of a blob upload whose bytes differ from the hash in its path, and of an undefined ?type= category on GET /models are this code.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text: Read each fault's location.field, compare the request with the route's schema in the protocol's OpenAPI document, correct the request and send it again.

Reader Kind Detail The domain's actor change_input Correct the field '{field}' as the route's schema requires, then send the request again. Any other reader change_input Pass this to the caller, who must correct the field '{field}' of the request.

docs.title: request.too_large
docs.text:

Type https://mthds.ai/errors/request.too_large Family request: The HTTP request itself, before any run. Domain input: the caller acts, by changing the request or its inputs Retry no: repeating the operation fails the same way HTTP status 413 Raised as a problem document, sent as the body of an HTTP response or kept in a run's record

docs.title: What it means
docs.text: The body, or a file in it, is larger than a size bound of the route. Each implementation sets its own bounds.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text: Make the request fit under params.limit. A method's large files can travel by hash to a runner whose GET /version declares blob_store: true, which keeps them out of the body.

docs.text:

Type https://mthds.ai/errors/request.idempotency_conflict Family request: The HTTP request itself, before any run. docs.text: An earlier request with the same idempotency key carried another body, so the runtime cannot treat this one as its repeat.

docs.title: request.idempotency_key_in_use
docs.text:
A request under this idempotency key is still running

Type https://mthds.ai/errors/request.idempotency_key_in_use Family request: The HTTP request itself, before any run. Domain runtime: nobody could have acted beforehand, so whoever made the call waits, retries or reports the problem Retry yes: repeating the operation may succeed, after retry_after seconds when the problem gives it HTTP status 409 Raised as a problem document, sent as the body of an HTTP response or kept in a run's record

docs.title: What it means
docs.text: An earlier request with the same idempotency key and the same body has not finished, so the runtime neither runs this one again nor has an answer to return yet.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text: Repeat the request unchanged, after retry_after seconds when the problem gives it. Once the first request has finished, the repeat returns its outcome.

docs.text: A hash entry of the request's files names bytes this runner does not hold, or the runner keeps no blob store at all, so it cannot assemble the method's tree. This is the protocol's own refusal of hash entries.

docs.text: Read params.missing_blobs. To a runner whose GET /version declares blob_store: true, upload each listed blob as POST /blobs/missing says; to any other runner, send each listed file inline. Then send the request again.

Any other reader change_input Pass this to the caller, who must upload each listed blob, or send its file inline if this runner keeps no blob store.

docs.text: A maybe-absent input or output is used where a value is required: it escapes through a step, a sequence or a condition whose boundary is not optional, a PipeCondition can continue without producing its output while that output is not ?, a template reads it without a guard, or a maybe-absent PipeParallel branch feeds a required structured field.

docs.title: run.timed_out
docs.text:
The run passed its time limit

Type https://mthds.ai/errors/run.timed_out Family run: A run's lifecycle and its reads. Domain method: the method's author acts, by changing the method Retry no: repeating the operation fails the same way HTTP status 422 Raised as a problem document, sent as the body of an HTTP response or kept in a run's record

docs.title: What it means
docs.text: The run did not end within the deployment's run time limit, so the method's work must shrink to fit it.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text: Split the method's work into smaller runs, or have it process fewer items per run.

docs.title: run.lost
docs.text:
The run's outcome is lost

Type https://mthds.ai/errors/run.lost Family run: A run's lifecycle and its reads. Domain runtime: nobody could have acted beforehand, so whoever made the call waits, retries or reports the problem Retry outcome_unknown: the operation may already have taken effect, so its outcome is learned before anything is repeated HTTP status 500 Raised as a problem document, sent as the body of an HTTP response or kept in a run's record

docs.title: What it means
docs.text: The run's execution can no longer be found, or never reported back, so the runtime holds no outcome for it. The run may have done its work, billed calls included, or may still be running, so a new run may repeat that work and is never started automatically.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text: Read the run again later, since an execution that has not reported may still end, and check what the run would have produced and the account's usage. Start a new run only once a repeat of the run's work is acceptable. If runs keep being lost, report it to whoever runs the runtime.

docs.text:

Reader Kind Detail The domain's actor read_run Read the run '{pipeline_run_id}' again later in case it reports how it ended, and start a new run only if repeating its work is acceptable. Any other reader read_run Read the run '{pipeline_run_id}' again later in case it reports how it ended, and start a new run only if repeating its work is acceptable.

docs.title: Detail
docs.text:

docs.title: run.outcome_unknown

docs.title: What it means
docs.text: The runtime sent the run on to be executed and lost the answer, so the run may have started, may have finished, or may never have begun.

docs.title: What to do

docs.text:

docs.title: runtime.unsupported
docs.text:
This runtime cannot do what was asked

Type https://mthds.ai/errors/runtime.unsupported Family runtime: The runtime itself. Domain operator: whoever runs the runtime acts Retry no: repeating the operation fails the same way HTTP status 501 Raised as a problem document, sent as the body of an HTTP response or kept in a run's record

docs.title: What it means
docs.text: The deployment lacks a capability the request needs, such as the asynchronous execution /start relies on.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text: Use a route or a form of the request that this runtime offers, such as /execute in place of /start, or a runtime that offers the capability.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
A problem carries the step aimed at whoever reads it: the first when its reader is the domain's actor, whoever runs the runtime, and the second for any other reader.

Reader Kind Detail The domain's actor fix_configuration Enable {capability} on this runtime. Any other reader change_input Send a request that does not need {capability}, or use a runtime that offers it.

docs.title: Detail
docs.text:
The problem's detail is written from this template, filled with the occurrence's parameters:

This runtime lacks {capability}, which the request needs.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Every parameter is present on every occurrence of the code.

Name Type Description capability identifier The capability the request needs.

docs.title: client.outcome_unknown
docs.text:
The call may have created a run

Type https://mthds.ai/errors/client.outcome_unknown Family client: What a client detects itself, and never receives as a response body. Domain runtime: nobody could have acted beforehand, so whoever made the call waits, retries or reports the problem Retry outcome_unknown: the operation may already have taken effect, so its outcome is learned before anything is repeated HTTP status none (client) Raised as an error a client detects itself, never received from a runner

docs.title: What it means
docs.text: The connection dropped, the call timed out, or the caller stopped it, after a request that creates a run had left, so the run may exist.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text: Read the run by its id when the client knows it. A client that knows no run to read leaves the outcome unknown and never repeats the request automatically, since a repeat may start a second run.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
A problem carries the step aimed at whoever reads it: the first when its reader is the domain's actor, whoever made the call, and the second for any other reader.

Reader Kind Detail The domain's actor read_run Read the run if its id is known, and otherwise leave the outcome unknown rather than send the request again automatically. Any other reader read_run Read the run if its id is known, and otherwise leave the outcome unknown rather than send the request again automatically.

docs.title: Detail
docs.text:
The problem's detail is written from this template, filled with the occurrence's parameters:

The connection was lost after a request that creates a run had left, so the run may exist.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
A parameter is present on every occurrence of the code unless it is marked optional, and one marked operator-only reaches only whoever runs the runtime, never a caller.

Name Type Description pipeline_run_id identifier (optional) The run, when the client learned its id before the connection was lost.

docs.title: client.follow_failed
docs.text:
Following a started run stopped

Type https://mthds.ai/errors/client.follow_failed Family client: What a client detects itself, and never receives as a response body. Domain runtime: nobody could have acted beforehand, so whoever made the call waits, retries or reports the problem Retry outcome_unknown: the operation may already have taken effect, so its outcome is learned before anything is repeated HTTP status none (client) Raised as an error a client detects itself, never received from a runner

docs.title: What it means
docs.text: The runtime acknowledged the run, and following it then failed, so the run has started and may still be going or may have ended. The call that started it has taken effect, so it is never repeated automatically.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text: Read the run by its id until it ends. Starting it again would run it twice.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
A problem carries the step aimed at whoever reads it: the first when its reader is the domain's actor, whoever made the call, and the second for any other reader.

Reader Kind Detail The domain's actor read_run Read the run '{pipeline_run_id}' by its id rather than start it again. Any other reader read_run Read the run '{pipeline_run_id}' by its id rather than start it again.

docs.title: Detail
docs.text:
The problem's detail is written from this template, filled with the occurrence's parameters:

The client stopped following the run '{pipeline_run_id}', which may still be going.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Every parameter is present on every occurrence of the code.

Name Type Description pipeline_run_id identifier The run.
